root_cause.text: The TCP timestamp offset generation in `secure_seq` had been downgraded to depend only on the host and not on the TCP ports, making the TS offset predictable enough for a SYN-cookie side channel to leak the source port.
root_cause.evidence: The patch explicitly says it “reverts 28ee1b746f49 (‘secure_seq: downgrade to per-host timestamp offsets’)” and that the fix is to “bring back TCP ports in TS offset randomization”; the diff changes `secure_tcp_ts_off()`/`secure_tcpv6_ts_off()` to `secure_tcp_seq_and_ts_off()`/`secure_tcpv6_seq_and_ts_off()` so `ts_off` is computed from `saddr`, `daddr`, `sport`, and `dport` instead of only addresses.

vuln_statements.content: u32 secure_tcp_ts_off(const struct net *net, __be32 saddr, __be32 daddr)

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The TCP timestamp offset generation in `secure_seq` had been downgraded to depend only on the host and not on the TCP ports, making the TS offset predictable enough for a SYN-cookie side channel to leak the source port.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch explicitly says it “reverts 28ee1b746f49 (‘secure_seq: downgrade to per-host timestamp offsets’)” and that the fix is to “bring back TCP ports in TS offset randomization”; the diff changes `secure_tcp_ts_off()`/`secure_tcpv6_ts_off()` to `secure_tcp_seq_and_ts_off()`/`secure_tcpv6_seq_and_ts_off()` so `ts_off` is computed from `saddr`, `daddr`, `sport`, and `dport` instead of only addresses.

intent_record.intent_summary: Introduce combined TCP sequence/timestamp-offset helpers and preserve the legacy sequence-only API via inline wrappers.
intent_record.what: The header adds an external declaration for init_net, defines a new union tcp_seq_and_ts_off containing u32 seq, u32 ts_off, and a u64 hash64 alias, replaces the old secure_tcp_seq/secure_tcpv6_seq prototypes with new secure_tcp_seq_and_ts_off() and secure_tcpv6_seq_and_ts_off() declarations that return the union, and adds static inline wrapper functions secure_tcp_seq() and secure_tcpv6_seq() that call the new functions with &init_net and return only ts.seq.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the TCP sequence generation API now computes and returns both the sequence value and timestamp offset together, allowing callers to reuse the same derived state instead of recomputing it separately. Existing callers of secure_tcp_seq() and secure_tcpv6_seq() still receive the sequence number through inline wrappers, preserving the old interface while routing through the new combined implementation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add the secure sequence header dependency so the file can use secure sequence helpers.
intent_record.what: A new header include, `#include <net/secure_seq.h>`, was added alongside the existing network-related includes.
intent_record.how: This makes declarations and inline helpers from `net/secure_seq.h` available to this translation unit, allowing it to use secure sequence generation functionality at compile time.

intent_record.intent_summary: Consolidate TCP request-socket sequence and timestamp initialization into a single callback returning both values.
intent_record.what: In `struct tcp_request_sock_ops`, the two function pointers `init_seq` and `init_ts_off` were removed and replaced with a single function pointer `init_seq_and_ts_off` that takes `const struct net *net` and `const struct sk_buff *skb` and returns `union tcp_seq_and_ts_off`.
intent_record.how: Callers of this ops structure will now obtain the initial TCP sequence number and timestamp offset together from one callback instead of invoking two separate callbacks, which changes the interface used during TCP request socket initialization and allows the implementation to compute and return both values in one step.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the unused `ts_secret` global declaration from the file.
intent_record.what: The diff removes the static global declaration of `siphash_aligned_key_t ts_secret` from the source file, leaving only `net_secret` defined in that section.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this change eliminates one unused or no-longer-needed secret key variable from the compilation unit, reducing available state but not introducing new behavior in the shown hunk.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the ts_secret initialization helper from this file.
intent_record.what: The static inline function ts_secret_init(), which called net_get_random_once(&ts_secret, sizeof(ts_secret)), was removed from the file. The net_secret_init() function remains unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this eliminates a separate initialization path for ts_secret, so that secret is no longer initialized by this function in this translation unit. Any code that previously relied on calling ts_secret_init() from here can no longer do so.

intent_record.intent_summary: Consolidate IPv6 TCP sequence and timestamp-offset generation into one helper that takes network context and returns both results together.
intent_record.what: The diff removes the separate IPv6 timestamp-offset helper `secure_tcpv6_ts_off()` and its export, and changes `secure_tcpv6_seq()` into a new function named `secure_tcpv6_seq_and_ts_off()` that returns a `union tcp_seq_and_ts_off` instead of a plain `u32`. The new function signature also adds a `const struct net *net` parameter. The shown body still builds a combined IPv6 address tuple from `saddr` and `daddr` and is being adapted to return both sequence-related data and timestamp-offset data from one helper.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the change consolidates IPv6 TCP secret-derived calculations so callers can obtain sequence and timestamp-offset information through a single function call rather than separate helpers. Adding `net` to the combined helper allows the timestamp-offset behavior to be controlled using the network namespace state during the same computation. This reduces duplicated hashing/setup work and changes the API surface by removing the standalone timestamp-offset export.

intent_record.intent_summary: Return a combined TCP sequence and timestamp-offset value, clearing the timestamp offset when timestamps are disabled.
intent_record.what: The function body was changed from using a local `u32 hash` and returning `seq_scale(hash)` to using a `union tcp_seq_and_ts_off st`, storing the SipHash result in `st.hash64`, conditionally zeroing `st.ts_off` when `net->ipv4.sysctl_tcp_timestamps != 1`, scaling `st.seq`, and returning `st`. The exported symbol name was also changed from `secure_tcpv6_seq` to `secure_tcpv6_seq_and_ts_off`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now produces a combined sequence/timestamp-offset value instead of only a scaled sequence number. When TCP timestamps are disabled or not explicitly enabled, the timestamp offset portion is cleared before returning, while the sequence portion still derives from the hashed 5-tuple and is scaled as before. This enables callers to obtain both a secure sequence value and a timestamp offset in one return path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Consolidate TCP sequence and timestamp offset generation into a single secure helper while preserving timestamp disable behavior.
intent_record.what: The separate function `secure_tcp_ts_off()` was removed, and `secure_tcp_seq()` was replaced by a new function `secure_tcp_seq_and_ts_off(const struct net *net, __be32 saddr, __be32 daddr, __be16 sport, __be16 dport)` that returns `union tcp_seq_and_ts_off`. The new function computes a 32-bit `ports` value from `sport` and `dport`, hashes `saddr`, `daddr`, and `ports` with `siphash_3u32()`, stores the result in `st.hash64`, conditionally clears `st.ts_off` if TCP timestamps are disabled, scales `st.seq` with `seq_scale()`, and exports the new symbol name `secure_tcp_seq_and_ts_off` instead of `secure_tcp_seq`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, TCP sequence number generation and timestamp offset derivation are now combined into one helper, so callers can obtain both values from a single hashed computation. The change preserves the timestamp-disable behavior by zeroing the timestamp offset when the sysctl is not enabled, while also producing a scaled initial sequence value from the same entropy source. This reduces duplication and centralizes the logic used for secure TCP initialization.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use a 4-tuple-aware secure timestamp offset when validating TCP cookie timestamps to correct timestamp handling.
intent_record.what: The code inside the timestamp-receipt adjustment path was changed from calling secure_tcp_ts_off(net, ip_hdr(skb)->daddr, ip_hdr(skb)->saddr) and using its return value directly, to calling secure_tcp_seq_and_ts_off(net, ip_hdr(skb)->daddr, ip_hdr(skb)->saddr, tcp_hdr(skb)->dest, tcp_hdr(skb)->source) into a union tcp_seq_and_ts_off variable, then extracting st.ts_off into tsoff.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the timestamp offset is now derived from a function that also incorporates the TCP source and destination ports, rather than only the IP addresses. This makes the computed timestamp offset more specific to the full 4-tuple of the connection, reducing the chance of reusing an incorrect offset and improving correctness when adjusting tcp_opt.rcv_tsecr.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a local TCP sequence/timestamp offset variable in `tcp_conn_request()` to support subsequent logic.
intent_record.what: A new local variable, `union tcp_seq_and_ts_off st;`, was added to `tcp_conn_request()` alongside the existing declarations near the start of the function.
intent_record.how: This change only introduces a declared stack variable in the function scope; by itself, the hunk does not alter control flow or runtime behavior, but it likely prepares the function to store or pass TCP sequence/timestamp offset state in later code.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the combined sequence/timestamp initialization helper during TCP request handling so the request timestamp offset is set correctly under the applicable connection setup paths.
intent_record.what: The code adds a pre-check that calls af_ops->init_seq_and_ts_off(net, skb) when timestamping is enabled or when neither a syncookie nor an initial sequence number is present, stores the result in st, and then changes the timestamp offset assignment from af_ops->init_ts_off(net, skb) to st.ts_off.
intent_record.how: This makes sequence-number and timestamp-offset initialization happen through a single helper path under the relevant connection setup conditions, ensuring the timestamp offset used for the request is taken from the combined initialization result instead of a separate timestamp-only call.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the precomputed sequence number from `st.seq` when handling TCP connection requests instead of reinitializing it.
intent_record.what: In `tcp_conn_request()`, the assignment to `isn` was changed from calling `af_ops->init_seq(skb)` to using the existing `st.seq` value.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the TCP connection request path now reuses the sequence number already stored in `st.seq` instead of recomputing it through the address-family-specific initializer, which changes how the initial sequence number is sourced for the request.

intent_record.intent_summary: Consolidate IPv4 TCP initial sequence and timestamp-offset generation into a single helper that returns both values together.
intent_record.what: The old helper `tcp_v4_init_seq(const struct sk_buff *skb)` returning a `u32` was removed, along with the separate `tcp_v4_init_ts_off(const struct net *net, const struct sk_buff *skb)` function. In their place, a new helper `tcp_v4_init_seq_and_ts_off(const struct net *net, const struct sk_buff *skb)` was added, returning `union tcp_seq_and_ts_off` and calling `secure_tcp_seq_and_ts_off(net, ip_hdr(skb)->daddr, ip_hdr(skb)->saddr, tcp_hdr(skb)->dest, tcp_hdr(skb)->source)`.
intent_record.how: This change consolidates initialization of the TCP sequence number and timestamp offset into one call, using both the network namespace and packet 4-tuple inputs together. At runtime, it enables generation of a paired sequence/timestamp-offset result from a single secure helper instead of computing them separately.

intent_record.intent_summary: Consolidate TCP sequence and timestamp-offset initialization into a single helper during IPv4 connect.
intent_record.what: Inside tcp_v4_connect(), the code that initializes tp->write_seq and tp->tsoffset in the non-repair path was changed to compute a single union tcp_seq_and_ts_off value via secure_tcp_seq_and_ts_off(...), then assign st.seq to tp->write_seq only if it is zero and assign st.ts_off to tp->tsoffset. The previous separate calls to secure_tcp_seq(...) and secure_tcp_ts_off(...) were removed.
intent_record.how: At runtime, TCP connection setup now derives the initial sequence number and timestamp offset from one combined helper using the same inputs, ensuring both values are generated together and consistently. This preserves existing behavior while reducing duplicated computation and keeping the sequence/timestamp initialization logically coupled.

intent_record.intent_summary: Consolidate IPv4 TCP request socket sequence and timestamp initialization into a single combined callback.
intent_record.what: In the IPv4 TCP request socket ops table, the separate .init_seq and .init_ts_off function pointers were removed and replaced with a single .init_seq_and_ts_off pointer assigned to tcp_v4_init_seq_and_ts_off.
intent_record.how: At runtime, IPv4 TCP request socket initialization now uses one combined callback to initialize both the initial sequence number and the timestamp offset together, instead of invoking two separate callbacks for those values.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the full IPv6 and TCP tuple to compute the timestamp offset during TCP cookie validation.
intent_record.what: The code in `cookie_tcp_check()` was changed so that, instead of calling `secure_tcpv6_ts_off()` to compute `tsoff`, it now declares a `union tcp_seq_and_ts_off st`, calls `secure_tcpv6_seq_and_ts_off()` with the IPv6 source/destination addresses plus the TCP destination and source ports, and assigns `tsoff = st.ts_off` before subtracting it from `tcp_opt.rcv_tsecr`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the timestamp offset used to adjust the received echoed timestamp is now derived from a security function that incorporates both the IPv6 tuple and the TCP port tuple, making the offset computation more specific to the connection and reducing the chance of accepting or validating a timestamp with incomplete context.

intent_record.intent_summary: Combine TCPv6 initial sequence and timestamp offset generation into one helper returning both values together.
intent_record.what: The old `tcp_v6_init_seq()` function returning a `u32` was removed, along with the separate `tcp_v6_init_ts_off()` function. In their place, a new function `tcp_v6_init_seq_and_ts_off(const struct net *net, const struct sk_buff *skb)` was added that returns `union tcp_seq_and_ts_off` and calls `secure_tcpv6_seq_and_ts_off(net, ipv6_hdr(skb)->daddr.s6_addr32, ipv6_hdr(skb)->saddr.s6_addr32, tcp_hdr(skb)->dest, tcp_hdr(skb)->source)`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, TCPv6 initialization now obtains the initial sequence number and timestamp offset together from a single helper instead of computing them separately. This consolidates the logic and ensures both values are derived consistently from the same net namespace and packet tuple, reducing duplicated computation and the risk of mismatched initialization.

intent_record.intent_summary: Consolidate TCPv6 sequence and timestamp offset initialization into a single helper call while preserving connect-time behavior.
intent_record.what: In tcp_v6_connect(), the code now computes a single union tcp_seq_and_ts_off value named st via secure_tcpv6_seq_and_ts_off(), passing the IPv6 source and destination addresses plus source and destination ports. The previous separate calls to secure_tcpv6_seq() and secure_tcpv6_ts_off() were removed. The write_seq assignment now uses st.seq, and tp->tsoffset is assigned from st.ts_off.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the TCPv6 connect path now derives the initial sequence number and timestamp offset together from one helper call instead of two separate helpers. This keeps the sequence and timestamp-related values consistent with each other for a given connection setup and preserves the existing behavior of only initializing write_seq when it is still zero.

intent_record.intent_summary: Consolidate IPv6 TCP request socket sequence and timestamp offset initialization into a single combined callback.
intent_record.what: In the IPv6 `tcp_request_sock_ops` structure, the separate `.init_seq` and `.init_ts_off` function pointers were removed and replaced with a single `.init_seq_and_ts_off` pointer assigned to `tcp_v6_init_seq_and_ts_off`.
